'''Pierre Sikivie''' (born 29 October 1949) is an American [[theoretical physicist]] and currently the Distinguished Professor of [[Physics]] at [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web | author=| title= Pierre Sikivie at University of Florida| url= http://www.phys.ufl.edu/faculty/sikivie.shtml | publisher= | year=}}</ref> He invented the axion haloscope<ref>{{cite web | author=Graham P. Collins| title= An experiment may have seen an elusive new particle| url= http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/a-hint-of-axions/ | publisher=Scientific American | year=2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | author=Rachel Courtland | title= The Hunt for the Invisible Axion | url= https://spectrum.ieee.org/the-hunt-for-the-invisible-axion | publisher=IEEE | year=2014}}</ref> and the axion helioscope<ref>{{cite web | author=Konstantin Zioutas| title= Let there be axions | url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29663 | publisher=CERN | year=2006}}</ref> and has played an important role in the development of axion cosmology.<ref>{{cite journal | title= Pierre Sikivie and the Gift for Simple Ideas | journal= American Institute of Physics Conference Series | volume= 1274 | issue= 1 | pages= 1–6 | year=2010| osti= 21426567 | doi= 10.1063/1.3489552 | series= AIP Conference Proceedings | last1= Van Bibber | first1= Karl | last2= Tanner | first2= David B. | last3= Van Bibber | first3= Karl A. | bibcode= 2010AIPC.1274....1V | hdl= 10945/60986 | doi-access= free | hdl-access= free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | author=Jon Cartwright | title= Axions could solve lithium problem | url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2012/feb/15/axions-could-solve-lithium-problem | publisher=Physics World | year=2012 }}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Sikivie completed his Licencie en Sciences from [[University of Liège]], Belgium in 1970 and completed his Ph.D. in [[Physics]] under [[Feza Gürsey]] from [[Yale University]] in 1975 with thesis ''Lepton and Hadron Spectra in Universal Gauge Theories''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://physics.yale.edu/pierre-sikivie | date = 29 January 2019 | title = Pierre Sikivie | publisher = Yale University Department of Physics | access-date = 22 January 2022 | archive-date = 22 January 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220122072829/https://physics.yale.edu/pierre-sikivie | url-status = dead }}</ref> He was a research associate at Dept. of Phys., Univ. of Maryland from 1975 to 1977 and at [[SLAC]] from 1977 to 1979. He became Senior Fellow at [[CERN]] from 1979 to 1981 and assistant professor at University of Florida from 1981 to 1984. He became an associate professor of physics at [[University of Florida]] in 1984, and promoted to professor in 1988. He received his present title of "Distinguished Professor" in 2012. He is the 2020 recipient of the [[Sakurai Prize]] and the 2025 recipient of the Galileo Galilei Medal.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.ggi.infn.it/galileomedal.html | title = The "Galileo Galilei Medal" Award | access-date = 27 February 2025}}</ref>

In 1994 Sikivie was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He was a Guggenheim Fellow for the academic year 1997–1998.<ref>[https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/pierre-sikivie/ Pierre Sikivie, John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]</ref> In 2026 he was elected to National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/ | title = National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members | access-date = 18 May 2026}}</ref>

== Dark matter axion physics ==
Sikivie played a crucial role in the development of the Axion Dark Matter eXperiment ([[ADMX]]). He collaborated with his colleagues, [[Neil S. Sullivan]] and [[David B. Tanner]], at [[University of Florida]] and developed the experimental details of ADMX.<ref> {{cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/28079|title=Results from a search for cosmic axions|accessdate= 30 January 2023}} </ref> In 1983, Sikivie, along with [[John Preskill|J. Preskill]], [[Mark B. Wise|M. B. Wise]], [[Frank Wilczek|F. Wilczek]], [[Larry Abbott|L. F. Abbott]], [[Michael Dine|M. Dine]], and [[Willy Fischler|W. Fischler]], discovered that cosmic axions created from mis-alignment mechanism can be a substantial fraction of Dark Matter. Later Sikivie laid the theoretical ground for dark matter axion detections such as the [[ADMX]].
